annotations.text:
A version of Lilo I think is better.

Ten screens, left to right in the order you would meet them. Home, then creating a trip, then the trip itself; the two halves of one input surface — Add anything, which reads a pasted confirmation, and Ask about it, which answers questions about the trip; then who's in, the money, the plan, saved places, and a second trip to show the system holding under a different photo.

Four arguments sit on the board below, and the apps each idea came from are credited there. Sample content throughout — names, times, prices and references are invented.
Money is new — and the argument for it is on the board below. Lilo already models parties with split bookings; this is the arithmetic that was missing, laid out the way Wise lays out a transfer.

Same layout, different trip.

The accent is derived from the cover: Amalfi's terracotta gives #98673E, Tokyo's dusk gives #188295. Both are darkened until they clear 4.5:1 on white, so the colour that identifies a trip is also safe to set type in — which retires the cyan contrast problem rather than patching it.
The case, in four parts, with sources. If you disagree with an argument, the screens it produced are wrong — start here rather than with the pixels.
